exclude: Boot screen and its padding at hand-over. The snapshot has the BASIC banner, blank cells and unchanged power-on fill at the end. The engine later reuses part of this range for runtime state.
Exact same-address remainder of the first G-LOADER load before relocation. All 256 bytes match its original tape data and the relocated loader is analysed in the title part.
Title speech wave workspace. A store watch during the title voice call stopped after $A7F7, and the same bytes persist into the engine hand-over.
3 parts: Scoreboard, Loading presentation, Final sequence
elsewhere: 3 parts: Scoreboard, Loading presentation, Final sequence

comments.text: The title loader jumps here after loading tape record 490. The jump transfers control to $2D8C to reset the CPU stack and enter the resident program.

Clear $6E/$6F and the 26 zero-page bytes at $84. Choose three or four raster ticks from the value in $9813, generate all 256 bit reversals at $FCC0 and give the mission its initial two 16-bit counters.

Prepare a new tower arrangement. Start with outer tower 7 and use $0BD1 to pick distinct room numbers for slots 1 through 3. Shuffle five entries at $0440, copy six candidates into the room records and derive two fields per room from the packed entries at $9AA6.

Set screen memory to $B800 in VIC bank $8000, write two lines of screen codes and scan the CIA keyboard matrix. Recognise the Y key as row mask $F7 with column value $FD and increment $9A4F to request a restored mission.
Twenty-one screen codes written to $B9C2 by $0A4A. This row asks whether to resume the saved game.
Twenty-one screen codes written to $BA12 beneath the first resume prompt row. The text shows the Y/N choice.

Build the tower arrangement, then use the saved-game path only when $A1D1 is zero. The cassette hand-over holds $01 there and skips that path. Initialize the raster display, load the tower resources and enter the elevator loop at $3A35.
Point the destination to $0440 and fill Y entries with A via $623F without modifying the fill value.
Generate a new byte via $3561, reduce it modulo the caller's accumulator value, return the remainder in A and restore X and Y.
Swap two randomly selected entries from $0440 for each iteration. A supplies the exclusive bound for both calls to $0BD1, and the outer repetition count begins at twelve.
A supplies a base offset. Add it to a random remainder below ten from $0BD1 and write the result at ($80),Y, advancing Y.

Preserve $9762 on the stack and switch off raster interrupts while the end sequence is prepared. Load three resources using tape table offsets $4B, $50 and $55, execute the overlay through its $7800–$780C jump table, then wait for fire.
Repeat the wait at $0C91 with Y counting down from 50, falling through into one final wait.
Take the current low raster line, decrement it and poll $D012 until that value appears. A caller can use this to wait for a raster wrap.
Compare the selected variant at $88E7 with the applied variant at $A191. If they differ, swap four pairs of 68-byte row groups and remember the new selection.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 2 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $0CA1.
Enter here after the compiler frame setup. A matching variant returns immediately, and a change calls $0CF7 for each of the four row group pairs.
Set up the compiler frame for a 68-byte exchange between two caller-supplied pointers.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 8 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $0CFD.
Read the two pointers from the compiler frame. Swap one byte at a time and advance both pointers until 68 bytes have been exchanged.
Set the selection timer to one, point zero-page address $5A at SID registers and write NOP at $1187 so the next melody call enters the player.
Replay the instrument's first seven bytes across the three SID voice blocks. Save each voice's gate pattern and copy four more settings into the SID global range.
Clear 25 consecutive SID registers and patch the melody entry at $1187 with RTS.
Runtime hook invoked by the scene raster handler. The opening floor snapshot holds RTS at this entry, and $2FDF preserves the first opcode while managing its wait state.
On expiration select an instrument and initialize it, then update the three voice patterns. Every sixteenth timer step advances $8DC3, which stops playback when it reaches $96.
Divide the elapsed count by 25 and index $9809 with the quotient. Copy the selected low and high instrument pointer bytes to $58/$59, then select three starting offsets and set their counters to one.

For each of three SID voices fetch the event-stream pointer and decrement its countdown. On zero read duration and note, advance that stream by two and write the indexed SID frequency. The count of one releases the gate.
Subtract the byte divisor in Y until the unsigned X:A dividend falls below zero. Return the remainder at $9B33 and the quotient at $9B34.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 8 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $161F.
Multiply the tower index at $86BA by 21. The record address starts at $8830 for variant 2 and $8836 for other variants.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 2 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $186B.
Run $18BF or $18B9 from bits 0 and 1 of the movement argument. Sample the returned bits again while calling the countdown update at $28C6 on each iteration.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 0 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $1C2E.
Inline selector table consumed by $2DA8. Add -1 to the original selector, use one of the 6 indexed target words when in range, and select $1CF5 otherwise.
Inline selector table consumed by $2DA8. Add -1 to the original selector, use one of the 6 indexed target words when in range, and select $1D9A otherwise.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 4 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $1DC6.

When the raster tick index is one, index $8489 with A and update the corresponding panel state. Flip $7FA7, advance $7FA8 on alternating eligible passes and use it to read the next value from the zero-terminated sequence at $8DF1.
Read X/Y byte pairs from the pointer at $30 until a zero X. Draw the same glyph in $32 at every pair through $3348 and advance the pointer by two each time.

Five-byte records used by $37A2. The first word is a number rendered into three decimal filename characters; the second is the load destination. The fifth byte is present in the table but the cassette entry at $37A2 does not read it.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 6 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $25F0.
Use the first argument to find a 21-byte tower record from $8828. Start at byte 8 of that record, set colour override 5 and begin drawing at screen row 17.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 0 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $27F5.

Subtract the current frame-rate threshold $9813 from elapsed ticks at $4C. After reaching the threshold update the current tower clock and the mission clock, then draw the three displayed time bytes through the pointer at $A31C when the elevator panel is active.
Run the screen transition, clear $23A3 and jump to the loader for the score program.

Subtract one from the seconds field. Signed underflow writes back 59, borrows from minutes and performs the same wrap before decrementing hours. The low-time path checks the other two fields before calling the warning routine.
Convert A through $99F5, set row $10 and pass the resulting character and the caller's X column to the screen writer at $3348.
Subtract one from the byte selected by Y in the three-byte record pointed to by $30 and store it back without altering Y.
Divide A by ten and return the quotient in A. Keep the remainder in $32 for the following units-digit draw.
Multiply outer tower number by the 21-byte record stride and add the base $8828, returning the resulting address in X:Y.
Multiply the outer tower number by ten, add $A334 and return the record address in X:Y.
Return zero in A and X and the constant one in Y.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 2 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $2A7F.
Refresh sprite state, set the enable mask from $A192 and store two input parameters at $893A. Wait for selection $0F to clear before polling again and dispatching through $2B19.
Inline selector table consumed by $2DA8. Add -1 to the original selector, use one of the 17 indexed target words when in range, and select $2B44 otherwise.
Convert outer tower number to the file name base by multiplying by 16 and adding 130, store the two-byte result at $233C and load the resource entry at index $0A.
Double the supplied room number into the low file number byte at $2332 and dispatch through the loader table's first slot.
Locate the destination record through $2A52 and copy $01A9 bytes from the returned X:Y address using $6217. Finish through the room decoder at $2BCA.
Select a display cleanup according to $8DE1, blank VIC output and call the loader with table offset $41. Set $0291 to $80 and call the overlay's entry at $A520.
Set the transition flag at $A1F3 and run $6A76, then reload tape block 490 with interrupts disabled. Run the loader's $BFFD tail and jump to the original game entry.
Clear decimal mode, bank I/O in with both ROMs out, pull the top two stack bytes into $88E5/$88E6, reset the software stack pointer to $023F and hardware stack to $FF, then jump to $0AD4.

Pull a pointer to the bytes following the call. Add the first inline word to $0A/$0B and compare against the second. For an in-range selector index the inline target table by twice the adjusted value; otherwise use the default pointer. Jump indirectly through $0A.

Pull the address of the inline frame descriptor, save $04–$09 on the hardware stack and copy the specified number of work bytes from $30 into the software stack. Synthetic return address $2E57 causes the inline routine's RTS to enter the restoration code.

Restore the working zero-page prefix from the frame if its saved length is nonzero. Restore pointers $04–$09, retrieve the original call site, drop the number of stack bytes specified by its inline descriptor and jump to the caller's continuation.
Disable VIC interrupt sources at $D01A, then read and write back IRQ status at $D019 to acknowledge the flags already set.

Configure the VIC interrupt source, select VIC bank $C000 by clearing CIA2 port A bits 0–1 and enable multicolour characters. Schedule the first raster event and install hardware IRQ $2F86 and NMI $2ED8.
Preserve A, X and Y, select I/O-visible RAM banking and restore the common RTI opcode from $2FBD at the NMI entry before transferring to $3012.
Preserve A and set $8DE1 to 3. The IRQ scheduler uses this value as the raster table index on wrap.
Preserve A and clear $8DE1. The IRQ scheduler uses index zero on wrap.
Select screen $F000 and character set $D800 via $D018=$C6. Copy scene colours from $9575/$9576 to the VIC multicolour registers, clear $6A and call the hook at $1187.
Delay by the short X countdown, then select screen $F000 and character set $D000 via $D018=$C4. Use fixed multicolours 6 and 14, signal the pocket band in $6A and wrap the tick count in $47 at $9762.
Advance the counters in $57, $4C and $47, wrap $47 at $9762 and increment $6B on the wrap. Prepare the sprite update for the index in $977A before joining the common IRQ tail.
Save A, X and Y on IRQ entry and dispatch through the writable jump at $2F8B. $2FC4 changes the two operand bytes to select the handler for the next raster event.

Test the stacked B flag before scheduling the next raster line. Acknowledge VIC flags, increment the schedule index, patch the next handler and sample CIA1 port B bit 7 before selecting the common exit.
Load the next raster index from $369C, reset it from $8DE1 when a zero raster-line entry ends the schedule and patch the IRQ jump at $2F8B from the split tables at $368C and $3694.
Stop CIA1 timer A, mask and acknowledge CIA1 interrupts, and enable VIC raster interrupts. Acknowledge pending VIC interrupts and clear the raster compare's high bit.
Look up the high and low parts of forty times the row through the tables at $32A3 and $328A, add column X and return the offset at $7C/$7D.
Low bytes of forty times each row from zero through 24, indexed by Y in $3279.
High bytes paired with $328A.

Reject coordinates outside a 40-by-25 character screen. Store the character at $F000 plus its row-major offset, choose a colour from the per-mode character tables when requested and write it to colour RAM. A readied clock trace stopped after the screen store at $32FB.
Save the character passed in A, set the option byte for the direct display path, and tail-call the bounds-checking writer with the supplied X and Y coordinates.
Save the character and clear the option controlling the secondary character-map copy before sharing the screen writer with $3348.
AND the two CIA1 port reads, invert the active-low result and mask to the five direction/fire bits. Write the mask to $86B9 and $9763 and return it in the two-byte result at $0A.
Set sprite zero to X $FE and Y $E4, install pointer $B8 in $F3F8 and set the sprite colours and multicolour mask. Clear the top X bit of sprites zero through four.
Copy A into the low return byte at $0A and clear X and the high return byte at $0B. Leave Y equal to one.
Reserve A bytes below software stack pointer $04/$05 and copy that many bytes from zero page $30 to the new frame. Restore the caller's Y before returning.
Restore A bytes to zero page $30 from the software stack and advance the frame pointer at $04/$05 by the same count.
XOR an indexed zero-page byte with the raster counter and the previous result at $83. Advance the zero-page index at $82, store the new result at $83 and return it at $0A while preserving X.
Set border and background to black. Clear five pages starting at screen $F000 and clear all 1000 visible colour cells starting at $D800.
AND both joystick-port bytes and test bit 4 until a fire button pulls it low. The loop returns with the masked accumulator zero.
Low bytes of the per-event IRQ targets used by $2FC4. The first two target $2F00 and $2F25 in the elevator.
High bytes paired with $368C when $2FC4 rewrites the IRQ dispatch operand.
Index incremented in $2F8E. $2FC4 reloads it from the display mode when the next raster entry is zero.
Low raster compare values for the IRQ schedule. Zero terminates each schedule; the elevator entries are $AA and $30.

Index the five-byte resource table at $2332 with X. Transfer its destination to $89/$8A, turn the 16-bit file number into three decimal characters using $37C8 and hand control to the cassette reader at $BE00.
Copy the working file number from $0E/$0F to $12/$13. Replace the copy with remainder modulo ten, divide the working number by ten and return the remainder plus $30 as the next filename character.
For X from $D0 down to one, expose the character ROM and read $CFFF+X, then expose RAM and copy to $E1FF+X. Leave I/O visible and X equal to $4F.
Zero-terminated REWIND string written into the screen by $3811 for the rewind prompt.
Zero-terminated WAIT string adjacent to the tape rewind message.
Eight values indexed by tower at $386B and cached in $9576 for the scene raster pass.
Eight values indexed by tower at $3865 and cached in $9575 for the scene raster pass.

Reset the current section marker, set up tower records and palette, then load the current tower's tape resource. Walk the room fields starting at offset 15; $40 skips a slot, and a populated byte contributes its low three bits to the room index table at $9C81.
Multiply the current tower at $86BA by 16 to select the tape's first file for that tower. Patch $2337 and dispatch via the resource-table entry at offset $05.
Resolve the destination room from X, multiply the input A by $01E0 and add $A500 for its source. Copy $01A9 bytes to the room record and pass it to the unpacker at $2BCA.
A single RTS in this cassette build. A second entry one byte later starts the separate $315 resource request.

Request tape resource table offset $23, then copy $0C pages from $A520 to $F400 using the shared backward copier. A $F400 store watch stopped after $6232 with the entire 3,120-byte resource intact at $A520.
Clear movement and display state before entering the elevator loop. Copy the two initial word values from $97AC and $9764 into their live fields, then tail-call the elevator display setup at $4068.

Read both sticks, mask input if $79 is set and dispatch separately when $8DE1 selects the room raster schedule. In the elevator, debounce fire through $73, handle the two vertical directions when both position checks pass and call the movement and rendering routines before the next input read.
Use the elevator position in $50 to look up its display position, update the lower panel through $1E88 and tail-call the elevator renderer at $28C6.
Zero the two high bytes, derive the first word from $50 and the direction sign in $4B, and derive the second from $54 plus the gap between $96 and $A3E9.

Set elevator display mode $0E in $48, copy the frame tick limit to $47 and reset the input latch, panel state and motion flags. Begin deriving the positions drawn by the panel from the mission's current location.

Write $6E to the high frequency byte of SID voice 1 and fall through to a separate path when it is already zero. Otherwise subtract two from $6E and, when nonzero, from $6F, then write the latter's old value to voice 2.
Compute a 9-bit target as sprite seven's Y plus 21. Substitute raster line 255 if $79 is nonzero, then wait for the raster to drop below that target and reach it again.
Compare $D012 to the low target at $71. Convert $D011 bit 7 into the raster high bit, then subtract $72 with the carry from the low comparison. Return carry set on or above the 9-bit target.

Clear $A3E5 and dispatch separately when the motion quantity in $49 is zero. Compare it against the previous value and when the repetition count reaches two, set the signed $4D step to $08 or $F8 according to the sign of $4B.
Index the shape base table at $46A5 with twice the pose at $48. Patch the absolute operands of the mirror loop to use three consecutive byte columns at that base.
Compare byte 63 of the first sprite with the requested direction at $4B. Update the flag and reverse the pixels only when it changes.

Look up each of the three bytes through the bit-reversal table at $FCC0, writing the outer bytes into opposite columns and the middle byte back into its own column. Walk backwards by three bytes per row.
Set full SID volume, choose one of two frequency words from the sign of $4B, then set voice three's ADSR and enable its noise waveform with gate.
Three pointer bytes used when the opening elevator installs idle agent sprites at $F3FD–$F3FF.
Three colour bytes installed for sprites 5–7 alongside the idle pointers.
Keep the screen at $F000 and select the character set at $E000 via $D018=$C8. Choose between the two draw paths by the flag at $8DC5.
Look up the current room index via $88E8, fetch its kind from $9C81 and apply the three corresponding table entries to $D021–$D023.
Copy the fixed checker glyph into $E780, then choose either a fifteen-entry glyph list or the later small-list path based on the supplied layout number.
For each of fifteen glyph IDs select a colour at $9CCD and an eight-byte shape at $9D54. Pack the shapes consecutively at $E788 and the colours at $8DB4.
Set the source pointer $7E/$7F from Y:X for the indexed copy routines.
Set the destination pointer $80/$81 from Y:X for the copy and fill routines.
Copy Y bytes from ($7E) to ($80) in descending index order, ending with index zero. Callers supply a nonzero count.
Copy X full pages plus Y additional bytes, working backward through indexed source and destination pointers. Y zero starts from the previous full page. Both pointers' high bytes are updated in place.
Write the input A into Y bytes at ($80) in descending index order, ending with index zero. A is unchanged.
Fill X full pages plus Y bytes with the supplied A. The loop uses the high byte of the destination pointer as a descending page counter.

Select the display setup from $8DE1, then draw the panel frame with repeated character rectangles. Before a restart, $A1F3 selects seven four-column strips with successive colours. The other path reads three-byte entries backwards from $88E2.
Add the supplied width and height to X and Y to form exclusive bounds. Use $3348 to fill the rectangle with the character in A and restart at the saved X for each row.
Clear the 64-byte sprite slot at $EC80, then copy seven bytes from $7C20. The seventh source byte is also the opcode at this entry point.
Six rows of three opening event offsets, one per SID voice. $11E9 chooses a row before initializing the event timers.
Low bytes of the three event stream pointers read by $11FF. Their initial values are $DA, $00 and $26.
High bytes of the first, second and third event-stream pointers at $7E07. They place the streams at $7EDA, $7F00 and $7F26.
Index used to choose a row of three initial event offsets at $7DF5.
$1188 decrements this count and selects a fresh instrument at zero. $11AB reloads it with $50.
Three per-voice offsets advanced by two after the player reads each duration and note pair.
One countdown per voice. A zero takes a new event, and one restores that voice's gate-control byte.
Three saved SID control patterns. The event player ORs in the gate bit when writing the next tone.
Low byte of the first word in the indexed SID frequency table. The entry for note $00 is zero, and the rising frequency sequence starts at note $0C.
High byte of the first SID frequency word. $1225 uses this base with twice the note number to select the high register value.
First voice's duration and note pairs. Its first event has duration $50 and note $39, before the next pair $14/$30.
Second stream selected by the pointer at $7E08/$7E0B. It starts with duration $50 and note $60, whose frequency word is zero.
Third voice's duration and note pairs. Its opening event uses the same zero-frequency note before the stream proceeds to note $18.
Seven low bytes, indexed by the instrument selection in Y at $11BC.
Seven $7F high bytes paired with the pointer lows. Each result points to an 11-byte instrument record beginning at $7F56.
Seven 11-byte records. Each supplies the common SID voice template followed by four bytes for global SID settings, copied by $113F.
Four little-endian pointers to the first left-side elevator panel rows at $91C0, $91D1, $91E2 and $91F3.
Eight pointers into the $8E90 series, each 17 bytes after the previous one. They select the middle elevator backdrop rows.
Four pointers to the lower row pattern beginning at $9248, with the final two referring to the same source row.
Four 17-byte strides from $9028, used by the alternate set of backdrop entries.
Eight pointers, from $8F18 to $8F8F, for a second middle backdrop pattern.
Five copies of the four-pointer sequence $9138, $9149, $915A and $916B. Consecutive source rows are 17 cells apart.
Four 17-byte row addresses from $9204. From the third cell in each row, the first fifteen characters match the right-side backdrop in the opening display.
The eight row addresses from the $8F18 series, repeated for the right-side section.
Four lower backdrop row pointers beginning at $927B. The final two reuse the $929D row.
Eight background colour values selected by the room kind in $9C81 and copied to $D021 by $58F3.
Eight values for $D022, indexed by the same room kind.
Eight values for $D023, loaded in the final colour store of $58F3.
Six marker glyph values cycling through $D3, $D4, $D5 and $D6. A zero terminates the cycle and makes $1E88 restart it.
Eight 17-character row templates pointed to by $87B0. Repeated plain wall, doorway and deck pattern codes form the central part of the opening elevator background.
Eight matching width templates for the opposite side, with separate edge cells.
Four 17-byte rows in the first variant of the group exchanged with $8FE4 by the call at $0CB8.
Alternate rows for the first group. This copy starts 68 bytes after $8FA0 and receives those rows during the exchange.
Four rows 17 bytes wide beginning at the second primary row-group pointer passed by $0CC3.
Alternate 68-byte row group for $9028. Its low pointer byte is the $6C pushed at $0CC2.
Third primary row group. The exchange at $0CDA starts here and includes the four consecutive rows up to $90F3.
Third alternate row group. It supplies the 68 bytes replacing $90B0 when the backdrop selection changes.
Final primary row group among the four exchanged by $0C9B. Its penultimate boundary is the start of the alternate at $917C.
Alternate of the final group. The last of its 68 bytes is $91BF, just before the next backdrop region.
Four 17-code rows from $91C0. Their first fifteen cells match columns 0–14 of the opening screen's first four tile lines.
The right-hand equivalent of the upper backdrop. Skip the first two cells to match the visible right crop at column 25.
Three distinct lower deck rows. The nearby row pointers reuse the last pattern to finish the block.
Three 17-code lower deck rows. The part beginning two characters in matches the screenshot's right edge region.
Nine lists of fifteen IDs for layout values 0 through 8. Each ID selects both a glyph shape and a colour. The layout-zero watchpoint ran to the end of this copy and all 120 output bytes matched.
Set to 50 by $08C5, or to 60 if the KERNAL's video-standard byte indicates the other timing. $28CE compares the elapsed tick count with it.
Eleven character codes for zero, one through nine and colon. The clock display indexes this table before writing the code into the pocket computer.
Literal glyph eight for the two punctuation locations in the countdown display.
One colour value per glyph ID. $5A1D uses each ID as the Y index into this table before filling $8DB4 and following.
Glyph ID zero in the panel bank. The layout lists use zero where the requested eight-byte shape is blank.
Glyph ID one alternates $55 and $AA. $59E7 copies it to $E780 independently of the layout, where it becomes glyph $F0 in the destination character set.
Shapes for IDs $02 through $86. $5A2B multiplies the ID by eight before adding $9D54. The special layout at $A1F4 includes the highest IDs in the bank.
Fifteen IDs applied by layout value $27. The first row starts with a blank and uses shape IDs $7C through $7E across the next three cells.
Sprite slots $00–$0F in VIC bank $C000. The rendered planes compose the agent's first four stride poses, with torso shapes at $C040, $C140, $C240 and $C340 and accompanying limb fragments.
Column 1 of the first sprite row. The generic mirror loop at $4A38 uses this operand before patching it to the selected shape base plus one.
Column 2 of the first sprite row. The generic mirror loop here exchanges the right and left byte columns, with the base patched at $49F6.
Sprite slots $10–$1F continue the running sequence and transition through upright poses. Torso and arm or leg fragments occupy separate slots so the renderer can position them independently.
Sprite slots $20–$2F start with standing body components, then include each curled or partly inverted somersault pose as separate body fragments.
Sprite slots $30–$3F complete the sequence of rotated limbs and upright figures used when the player returns to a standing pose.
The 256 eight-byte glyphs selected when the panel raster pass stores $C4 at $D018 in VIC bank $C000. This set supplies digits, the pocket display graphics and small labels.
Glyphs $80–$FF of the $D000 character set. They include paired geometry, border components and compact label fragments.
The 256 eight-byte glyphs selected when the upper raster pass writes $C6 to $D018. The VIC reads RAM here while the CPU generally sees colour RAM and the CIAs at these addresses.
Glyphs $80–$FF of the $D800 character set. The VIC reads these tile shapes from RAM under the two CIA register pages.
Glyphs $00–$7F in the alternate character set. Screen base remains $F000 when $50C0 writes $C8 to $D018.
Operand base of the character ROM copier. The indexed store uses offsets 1 through $D0, so the glyph byte at the base itself is preserved.
Start of the 208 bytes replaced by character ROM data when $37F6 runs. The copy supplies 26 character cells before the prompt draws.
Glyph RAM beyond the end of the 26-cell prompt-font copy. This part of the alternate source character set is retained.
The last 18 glyphs in the portion of the alternate character set supplied by record 267. The last complete eight-byte cell ends at $E48F.
Multicolour sprite slots $A0–$AB. Rendering the two-bit pixels reveals a round robot facing in multiple directions from these poses.
Multicolour sprite slots $AC–$B7. The low tracked base stays similar as the arm changes from horizontal to upright and folds again.
The routine at $7C26 replaces all 64 bytes. A store watch stopped after $7C2A and execution to $7C3B left F0 F0 F0 0F 0F 0F A2 followed by 57 zero bytes.
Sprite slots $B8–$BF include the distinct blob at $EE00 and later variants of the tracked chassis with different upper silhouettes.
This address starts the end of tape record 306, present before game initialization. The engine later overwrites the visible screen at $F000.
